title: The video mocks are the user's again, and D18 is gone
goal: Commit 72a2a75c (2026-09-19, 'Video, drawn against the app that exists') and the later fourteen-pages task rewrote the user's video mocks to fit the code the loop already had: tracks removed, the Layers group argued away, and UX-PATTERNS D18 invented to replace tracks with layer rows. The user rejected the result on 2026-09-23 and wants real tracks. Restore the user's intent before anything else is built against these pages. Target: the user's mocks (docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html, video-shell.html, comp-video.html and the page named here) at their fidelity; runner-prompt rules on default config, side-by-side with the mock, labels-not-explanations and right-click apply. Ask throughout: would a Premiere editor get this, and is it easier here?
notes: Filed from the 2026-09-23 video audit in the intake window.
acceptance: Every change 72a2a75c and the fourteen-pages task made to docs/design/mocks/pages/video*.html, video-shell.html and comp-video.html is listed, and each one that removed or weakened something the user drew (tracks, track headers, grouping, audio lanes, the Layers group, the transport row) is reverted
UX-PATTERNS D18 is rewritten: a document with time has real tracks (video, audio, captions, titles), named, renamable, groupable, each holding many clips, and a layer can move between them
docs/design/video-surface.md and video.md no longer say video needs almost no new chrome or reuse the timing strip; they point at the restored mocks as the target
No Swift code changes in this task
